cohort: 5710 pregnant women with a gestational age greater than 28 weeks
finding: Placenta previa and placenta accreta were the two most frequent risk factors for postpartum haemorrhage, with varying risk factors depending on the number of fetuses and mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Multifetal gestation was a risk factor for PPH regardless of mode of delivery; multiparity was a potential cause of PPH in singletons and caesarean sections, but suggested a lower incidence in vaginal deliveries; macrosomia increased PPH incidence in vaginal/singleton deliveries; and preeclampsia increased PPH risk in vaginal deliveries.
